title: Label the meaning
summary: Axis labels explain what values mean and which units they use. A title tells the reader the chart's topic.
introduction: Axis labels explain what values mean and which units they use. A title tells the reader the chart's topic. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Axis labels explain what values mean and which units they use. A title tells the reader the chart's topic.

blocks.code:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot([1, 2, 3], [2, 4, 3])
ax.set_xlabel("Day")
ax.set_ylabel("Books read")
ax.set_title("Reading this week")
plt.show()
blocks.title: Label the meaning

blocks.text: The chart now explains both axes. A reader does not need to guess whether 4 means books, minutes or people.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Change the data to minutes and update the label.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A chart without units can be misleading even if its points are correct.
For more detail later, use this [Matplotlib further reading](https://matplotlib.org/stable/users/explain/quick_start.html).
